# Provenance: how this tree relates to the sealed research epoch

This directory is a clean-room re-packaging of the environment that produced
the sealed research epoch `hardened-v6-aecadda` (runtime commit
`aecadda60f795293c18d24d04ac91fe66b0a2278`, packaging commit
`59b05c194f0b28c61ed6608b89c7ecbd9a3a0f2d`, sealed 2026-10-10). The sealed
packet is identified by `sha256(SHA256SUMS) =
1290c7fa9a364ac8db4dcb005d305f18183574273581099878a211267f58977f`; its
source archive is `source.tar.gz =
8be1c36c134103f1daf907625a98d5d9ce3f74b1cb2160c62e4075eb4855fbb3` (399
members). Both were verified before this tree was built.

## What changed, and why

| File | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `data/service.json` | Source M keeps its record but its locator, locator-record and table digests are withheld; S7 and S8 keep their records without their document and proposal-record digests; the qualification sentences say so. Entries unchanged | The private digests are not published (see `THIRD-PARTY.md`) |
| `data/labor-v2.json` | The S7 citation record without its private document digest; durations and citations unchanged | Same |
| `data/human-time-policy-v3.json` | Regenerated from the published labor table | Derived file |
| `removal-policy/job-checklists.json` | 625 basis `path` strings respelled from a machine-local shared folder to `benchmark-policy/<document>` | No host paths in the public tree |
| `tools/l1_controls.py` | `CHECKLIST_SHA256` pinned to the respelled checklist (`f98311db...`) and written as `reassembly.source_raw_sha256`; sealed pin kept in a comment | Follows the file above |
| `tools/repair_controls.py` | `example_config()` reads `data/labor-v2.json` instead of the unshipped v1 `data/labor.json` | The v1 labor table carried manual page references and was never part of the sealed source set |
| `configs/V1..V5.configuration.json` | Regenerated by the shipped generator from the inputs above | The sealed configurations embed the service corpus, the labor table and the checklist |
| `epochs/amended-v5/` | The 18 modules, bootstrap and manifest of the amended runtime `24a5713`, byte-identical to its sealed source set | Replays the published V1 reference and exploratory records |
| `tests/` | 39 of the lane's 60 modules ported, plus `test_headgasket_cli.py`; see below | Public tree |
| `headgasket/`, `bin/headgasket-mcp` | New | A working entry point |

The configurations shipped in `configs/` are byte-identical to the
configurations embedded in every published record under `../runs/` (the 13
scripted family records, the V1 reference and the exploratory model runs),
and `python3 -m headgasket prepare` regenerates them byte for byte:

| Variant | Public pin | Sealed pin (not shipped) |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | `a4e22f01d85b799e0bb92b90c56d423e792a56b5134750c6aa4d4edf9b6e232e` | `e2b962f610544b320c40c08927da3c26743c9fb9c8a71bcd1c985a0b45b07984` |
| V2 | `bf1726c9fa62f97d602f13c5d2483e9a59555632f5f37d493245e82d82ce679f` | `7db45e736f4cdc43d4bea39510925a2fec83925077888a5e397a7985de7b11da` |
| V3 | `a210cc8d19ffbe4b3e8d84f375d2fe7ecfa53872b2386d16ba98680ce81d4b5d` | `14baad9b2777dd6d0a0040895089a63aa9af31013b64048e2d57207b12882838` |
| V4 | `797d52ba162e5c52dc36f954b9c6d57c237bd9377279983a6bd0480d462cb9fa` | `86eb260afb3ca41205a2894e8ecd0060173d72d5a566027ddeb53aeb7b3f80da` |
| V5 | `f7783d4e19f3cf9dccf2b28ad35d48c35ca4d6e39911913d709b26521baea998` | `e9a89021fc38af83e5113f3f1e5d8e284a6b670a9c8545df68828967c06e4ea3` |

The public configuration of each variant is the sealed configuration with
exactly these changes: the 625 shared-folder citation paths respelled to
`benchmark-policy/<document>`; the private digests of sources M, S7 and S8
withheld and their two qualification sentences reworded; the reviewed
reference script re-pinned to the published corpus
(`repair_scoring.reference.service_sha256`, `repair_scoring.reference_sha256`);
and three derived digests recomputed over the published inputs: the analyst
time policy's `labor_content_sha256` and S7 `labor_source_record_sha256`, and
the checklist's `source_raw_sha256`. The first public derivation of the
records (made before this package was assembled) had kept those three derived
digests at their sealed values; the independent scorer refuses such a record
(`labor-policy`: the policy must be derived from the labor table it ships
with), so the records were derived once more against these configurations.
Both derivations replay the sealed action journal through the sealed runtime
of the record's epoch, and both were checked to differ from their input in hash
fields only. `../runs/RECORDS.md` section 5 lists every record's public and
sealed hashes.

Every published record replays and verifies here without
`--allow-unlisted-config`: from this directory,
`python3 -m headgasket replay --record ../runs/<set>/<case>/run.json` and
`python3 -m headgasket verify --run ../runs/<set>/<case>`. Records made with the
sealed configurations replay here only with `--allow-unlisted-config` (the
runtime is identical; their configuration hash is not a public pin).

## Launcher changes after the first package

- Runtime epochs: `replay` and `verify` select the runtime by the source
  manifest the record names, the current one or a pinned epoch in
  `configs/PINS.json` (`epochs`); `pins --check` verifies every epoch's files.
- `verify` checks `finish-record.json` when present and reports `absent`
  otherwise (the published records omit the copy); `validate` needs
  `run.json`, `actions.jsonl` and `report.json`.
- A record made with a different CPython version is refused with a named
  reason before replay (the interpreter version is part of the recorded
  source identity).

## The entry point and the DIRECT_SERVER_BLOCKER

In the sealed source, three entry points refuse unconditionally:
`tools/source_server.py main()`, `hgj.mcp.run_manifest()` (through
`SourceRuntime.require_deployment()`) and `SourceRuntime.replay_manifest()`.
They raise `DIRECT_SERVER_BLOCKER` ("Managed process control remains
unqualified after owned-child EPERM; source-bound server/replay start
withheld"), a hold that belonged to the research sandbox, where the host
could not prove it could stop a child process it had started. The hold was
never about the environment's own correctness, and it was never on the path
that produced the sealed records: those were produced by
`tools/variant_demo.py --worker serve|replay`, which constructs a
`SourceRuntime`, activates it, and calls `hgj.mcp.serve(Game(config,
source_runtime=runtime), stdin, stdout, out)` and `hgj.game.replay(record,
source_runtime=runtime)` directly.

The public launcher (`headgasket/cli.py`) takes exactly that path. It does
not modify `tools/source_server.py`, `hgj/mcp.py` or any pinned module (their
hashes are part of the record identity, so modifying them would make every
sealed record unreplayable). What replaces the refusal is the check the
loader already performs before any environment code runs:

1. the source manifest's raw hash must equal the pin in `configs/PINS.json`;
2. every one of the 18 modules and the bootstrap must hash to its manifest entry;
3. the configuration's raw hash must equal its pin (or the pin you supply with
   `--config-pin`).

Why the record format and the hash chain are unchanged: the record is written
by the pinned `hgj/mcp.py serve()` and `hgj/game.py export()`; the launcher
only chooses the configuration, the output folder and the streams. The
`environment_source` identity in each record is computed by the pinned loader
from the same 19 hashes, so a public record carries the same identity as a
sealed one (`source_manifest_sha256 = f347b0c8...`). The chain
(`previous_action_sha256` from `config_sha256`, `pre_/post_state_sha256`
per row) is computed inside `Game.call`, untouched. The thirteen sealed
family records replay byte for byte through the public `replay` command (see
`../runs/RECORDS.md`), which is the proof that nothing on the scoring path
moved.

`python3 -m hgj.mcp` and `python3 tools/source_server.py` still refuse, as
sealed; the tests keep the checks that they do (`tests/test_source_runtime.py`).

## Tests

The lane carried 60 test modules (489 tests, red at the sealed head: 61
errors and 4 failures, mostly from a stale 11-module closure list). Ported
here: 39 modules plus a new launcher test module, 323 tests, all passing on CPython 3.12.3 with 96 skips (the
Amendment 1 "pure helper" checks in `tests/test_amendment_controls.py`,
which need a reference scorer that is not part of this release).

Adaptations: `tests/test_source_runtime.py` lists the full 18-module closure
and asserts it equals the loader's, the emitter's and the shipped manifest's;
its check of the sandbox-only `tools/replay.py` utility is dropped.
`tests/test_finish_compact.py`, `tests/test_variant_controls.py`,
`tests/test_repair_demo.py` and `tests/test_procedure_transport.py` write to
the interpreter's temporary directory instead of into the tree.
`tests/test_human_time.py`, `tests/test_human_time_variants.py` and
`tests/test_service.py` read `labor-v2.json` (citing S7, as sealed); three tests that compared against the unshipped v1 labor table or
sandbox evidence are dropped with a note in place. The authored fixture in
`tests/test_repair_demo.py` was brought to the hardened finish contract
(compact summary reply) and one stale test in `tests/test_finish_admission.py`
(a synthetic soak PASS that the procedure epoch no longer produces, failing in
the lane too) is dropped with a note.

Not ported (sandbox-only): the seal/packet/guard tooling tests
(`test_seal`, `test_seal_selection`, `test_packet`, `test_guard`), the
receiving-pipeline tests for joint, soak, routes, supply, geometry and
provenance (`test_*_receiving`, `test_route_collection`,
`test_constituent_routes`, `test_ordered_provenance`,
`test_bolt_length_projection`, `test_source_endpoint`,
`test_joint_supplement`), and the tests of helper tools that are not shipped
(`test_control_sources`, `test_source_control_dispatch`,
`test_mcp_control_checks`, `test_mcp_fixture_demo`,
`test_mcp_soak_diagnostic`, `test_repair_accuracy_controls`,
`test_service_fixture_controls`).

## Hygiene scan

Before release the tree was scanned for host directory spellings, account
and owner names, product tokens, engine-maker names and credential patterns
(`work/scan_tree.py` in the publishing record). Hits in the public tree: the
client and provider names used as labels in `README.md`, the phrase "SOHC"
in the engine description, and the English word "gates" in one test. No host
paths, no account or owner names, no maker names, no tokens.
